mcqs.question: What is the definition of average power in the context of work and energy?

options.A: Average power is the total work done divided by the total time taken.
options.B: Average power is the force applied multiplied by displacement.
options.C: Average power is the energy stored per unit mass.
options.D: Average power is the rate of change of momentum.

mcqs.answer: Average power is the total work done divided by the total time taken.
mcqs.explanation: Average power (P_avg) is defined as the work done (W) divided by the time interval (t) over which the work is done, i.e., P_avg = W/t. Option A states this definition correctly; the other options describe unrelated quantities.

mcqs.question: How is instantaneous power related to the force acting on a particle and its instantaneous velocity?
mcqs.explanation: Instantaneous power is the product of the instantaneous force (F) and the instantaneous velocity (v) of the point of application, P = F·v. Option A expresses this relationship. Options B, C, and D are not correct formulations of instantaneous power.

mcqs.question: A worker lifts a 20 kg box through a vertical height of 5 m in 2 s. What is the average power delivered by the worker? (Take g = 9.8 m/s²)
mcqs.explanation: Work done = mgh = 20 kg × 9.8 m/s² × 5 m = 980 J. Average power = work/time = 980 J / 2 s = 490 W. Option A is correct; the other options arise from incorrect division or omission of the factor g.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate power to force and velocity
mcqs.question: A car engine exerts a constant force of 4000 N on a car moving at a constant speed of 20 m/s. What is the power output of the engine?
mcqs.explanation: Power = force × velocity = 4000 N × 20 m/s = 80,000 W = 80 kW. Option A matches this calculation. The other options correspond to incorrect multiplication or unit conversion errors.

mcqs.question: A 1500 J battery discharges completely in 5 s. What is the average power supplied by the battery during this interval?
mcqs.explanation: Average power = energy transferred / time = 1500 J / 5 s = 300 W. Option A is correct; the other options result from dividing by wrong time values or halving the result.

mcqs.question: A cyclist applies a pedaling force of 150 N while his bike moves at an instantaneous speed of 6 m/s. What is the instantaneous power output of the cyclist at that moment?
mcqs.explanation: Instantaneous power = force × velocity = 150 N × 6 m/s = 900 W. Option A is correct. Options B, C, and D arise from using only one of the quantities or incorrect arithmetic.

mcqs.question: A 10 kg block is pulled across a horizontal surface with a constant force of 50 N. It moves 20 m in 4 s. Assuming the force is in the direction of motion, what is the power developed?
mcqs.explanation: Work done = force × displacement = 50 N × 20 m = 1000 J. Power = work / time = 1000 J / 4 s = 250 W. Option A is correct. Option B (500 W) is a common mistake where students mistakenly divide by 2 s; option C and D are other incorrect divisions or using work as power directly.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate power to force and velocity
mcqs.question: Two objects move with the same speed of 10 m/s. Object A experiences a force of 30 N in the direction of motion, while Object B experiences a force of 60 N in the same direction. Which statement is correct regarding their power?

options.A: Object B has twice the power of Object A.
options.B: Both objects have the same power because their speeds are equal.
options.C: Object A has twice the power of Object B.
options.D: Power cannot be compared without knowing the masses of the objects.

mcqs.answer: Object B has twice the power of Object A.
mcqs.explanation: Power = force × velocity. Since both have v = 10 m/s, power_A = 30 N × 10 m/s = 300 W and power_B = 60 N × 10 m/s = 600 W. Thus Object B’s power is double that of Object A, making option A correct. Options B and C ignore the force difference, and D is irrelevant because power depends on force and velocity, not mass.
